Declare measurement

Source: R/declare_model.R
declare_measurement.Rd

Records what the study observes: the measured outcome, typically Y revealed from the potential outcomes given the assignment Z. Columns are added to the data the way declare_model() adds them, without a new ID column.

Usage

declare_measurement(..., label = "measurement", draws = 1L)

Arguments

...

(optional) Named arguments forwarded to fabricatr::fabricate(). Unquoted expressions are evaluated lazily in the caller's environment with access to the current data frame.

label

(optional) Step label. Defaults to "measurement".

draws

(optional) Number of nested draws for this step. Defaults to 1. When > 1, the step is re-executed draws times for each upstream draw during nested simulation.

Value

A design_step (class c("design_step", "dd", "function")): a function that takes the current data frame and returns it with the declared columns added. Add it to a design with +.

See also

Other design declarations: declare_assignment(), declare_estimator(), declare_inquiry(), declare_model(), declare_notes(), declare_parameters(), declare_sampling(), declare_step(), declare_test()

Examples

design <-
  declare_model(N = 100, U = rnorm(N), Y_Z_0 = U, Y_Z_1 = U + 0.5) +
  declare_assignment(Z = sample(rep(0:1, length.out = N))) +
  declare_measurement(Y = Y_Z_0 * (1 - Z) + Y_Z_1 * Z)

head(draw_data(design))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#>   ID         U  Y_Z_0  Y_Z_1     Z      Y
#>   <chr>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <int>  <dbl>
#> 1 001   -1.06  -1.06  -0.563     0 -1.06 
#> 2 002    1.63   1.63   2.13      0  1.63 
#> 3 003    0.541  0.541  1.04      1  1.04 
#> 4 004    1.46   1.46   1.96      0  1.46 
#> 5 005   -1.93  -1.93  -1.43      0 -1.93 
#> 6 006   -0.880 -0.880 -0.380     0 -0.880
